claims.explanation: Penfluridol's selective killing is best explained by its recently identified activity as a direct inhibitor of the glycolytic enzyme PFKL (and possibly other glycolytic/calcium-dependent targets), so lines with high glycolytic flux and high PFKL expression are most sensitive, while low-glycolytic or neuroendocrine/ALK-driven lines are relatively resistant. The enrichment of TP53 and PI3K/AKT-pathway mutations among sensitive lines is consistent with reliance on glycolysis and impaired ability to survive metabolic stress, whereas resistant lines include ALK-fusion neuroblastomas and other low-glycolytic tumors.

features.basis: Penfluridol directly binds and inhibits PFKL; PFKL is required for its anticancer activity (PMID 35530161)
TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines, consistent with loss of metabolic stress response
PI3K pathway activation drives glycolysis and is enriched in sensitive lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and glycolysis, enriched in sensitive lines
KRAS-driven tumors are glycolytic and appear in several sensitive lines
BRAF mutations drive MAPK-dependent glycolysis and appear in sensitive lines
ALK-altered neuroblastoma lines are among the least affected
NF1-mutant lines appear in both groups but several resistant lines carry NF1 loss
Penfluridol is annotated as a T-type calcium channel blocker targeting CACNA1G
Penfluridol antagonizes calmodulin-dependent enzymes, which could affect calcium signaling
Penfluridol downregulates integrin alpha6 signaling in TNBC (PMID 26627008)
Penfluridol downregulates integrin beta4 signaling in TNBC (PMID 26627008)
